tags.gist: Lists hoped-for benefits from patient participation to reduced administrative burden, while insisting innovation in care must begin with safety.
Wants risk assessed on real conditions of use such as reversibility, urgency, vulnerability, error detection, scale and staffing, counting both missed and unnecessary warnings.
Says benchmarks by themselves do not suffice for systems influencing diagnosis, triage or treatment; high-risk systems need prospective validation in varied patients and settings.
Wants the human-AI team including nurses evaluated for hallucinations, automation bias, cognitive burden and near misses, compared against adequately staffed care.
Says AI should support rather than displace clinical relationships, and clinicians need the ability to question, override and stop unsafe recommendations without retaliation.
Says AI must never replace safe staffing; people should be told when AI shapes their care and who is accountable, and disclosure is not consent.
Calls monitoring essential but says it must add to strong premarket evidence rather than replace it, so patients do not become involuntary test subjects.
Wants monitoring to cover subgroup performance, adverse events, near misses, changing errors and protected frontline reporting.
Says a machine must never serve as the only supervisor of another machine.
Says manufacturers must stay responsible for surveillance, correction and transparent communication.
Wants every output traceable to a model version, material changes caught before affecting care with revalidation and FDA review, and prompt suspension and rollback controls.
Says agentic systems that plan, act or interact with other systems warrant a stricter standard because errors can spread before anyone can intervene.
Wants a balanced framework with proportionate pathways requiring strong evidence, transparency, accountability and enforceable safeguards when stakes are high.
Says human alignment must come first and those who profit from AI must not shift its risks onto patients, families and clinical teams.
